# Keep people in control of agent work

Agent work shows its plan before acting, keeps pause, stop, and steer as primary controls, gates approvals by risk, streams a legible action record, notifies only when input is needed or something went wrong, and makes dismissal and correction cheap.

## Why

External standard, not learned from the user's feedback. People supervise agents by exception; they need to see intent before risk, intervene at any moment, and fix a wrong turn without restarting.

## Prefer

- Show the intended plan before consequential or long-running work begins.
- Keep pause, stop, and steer visible and reachable while the agent runs.
- Ask for approval in proportion to risk; let low-risk steps run.
- Show a readable stream of actions and outcomes the user can scan later.
- Notify only when the agent needs input, fails, or finishes something the user is waiting on.
- Let the user dismiss, undo, or correct a suggestion or step in one action.

## Avoid

- Approval prompts for every step regardless of risk.
- Stop or steer controls hidden in menus while work is running.
- Notifications for routine progress.
- Opaque runs whose actions cannot be reconstructed.

## Use when

- A surface starts, monitors, approves, or reviews autonomous agent work.

## Do not use when

- A single, instant, reversible suggestion where a plan and action stream add only noise.

## Sources

- Microsoft HAX Toolkit: Support efficient correction — https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/haxtoolkit/guideline/support-efficient-correction/
- Shape of AI: Action plan — https://www.shapeof.ai/patterns/action-plan
- Shape of AI: Stream of thought — https://www.shapeof.ai/patterns/stream-of-thought

## Check

- Can the user see the plan before risky or long work starts?
- Are pause, stop, and steer reachable while the agent runs?
- Are approvals proportional to risk, and notifications limited to input needed or exceptions?
- Can a wrong step be corrected or dismissed in one action?
